title: Gilding the Rose: Refactoring-Driven Development - Kevlin Henney - ACCU 2023
summary: Kevlin Henney works the Gilded Rose kata to argue for refactoring-oriented development: legacy is technical neglect, tests are documentation for people, small steps, and position code so the feature becomes trivial.

assertions.quote: technical debt is not your problem technical neglect is your problem that's the course

verdicts.note: A reframing consistent with debt-interest models but not separately testable.

assertions.quote: we have 20 years of evidence that tells us it was never the tool it was the mindset

verdicts.note: Tool-usage studies show refactoring tools are underused, which supports the mindset explanation.

assertions.quote: a failing test you tell exactly what is wrong quickly without have you having to spend a lot of time analyzing the failure
never trust a test you haven't seen file

verdicts.note: Mutation testing routinely finds tests that cannot fail; seeing the red state is the standard guard.

assertions.quote: if you make a mistake it's easy to find the bug yeah just work in small steps

verdicts.note: Core of Fowler's refactoring method; supported by practitioner evidence more than experiments.

assertions.quote: one commit in 30 is actually something that changed the behavior

verdicts.note: Describes a workflow; the ratio is one practitioner's anecdote.

assertions.quote: here is not typing typing is not the bottleneck it is understanding
let's refactor the control problem refactor on its own terms before migrating it to another Paradigm
